rv.q: This is a reminder that even solid-gold hits tarnish with time.
This revival, arriving at Trafalgar theatre after a tour, proves disappointingly forgettable.
In this iteration at least, it feels sluggish and lethargic.
It’s quirky, swift, ingenious and altogether a smashing hour and three quarters in the theatre.
It’s no mystery why this affectionate parody is still delighting audiences.
Patrick Barlow’s parody The 39 Steps creaks and groans in places but still has plenty of laughs.
That they still work today is testament to the power of clowning and physical theatre, without massive technological bells and whistles, to amuse and delight.

cn.t: This Hitchcock spoof revival draws mixed reactions—some find it a joyful, hilarious romp showcasing ingenious stagecraft, while others deem it tired and lacking precision compared to newer successors like Operation Mincemeat.
